title: Scientific Opinion on Dietary Reference Values for vitamin E as α‐tocopherol
authors: EFSA Panel on Dietetic Products, Nutrition, and Allergies (NDA)
funder: European Food Safety Authority, on request from the European Commission (Question No EFSA-Q-2011-01231); adopted on 11 June 2015.
result: The Panel considers vitamin E as α-tocopherol only. Absorption of tocopherols and tocotrienols resembles that of other lipids, and the main fraction is secreted in chylomicrons. In hepatocytes, the α-tocopherol transfer protein preferentially binds α-tocopherol rather than other tocopherols or tocotrienols and incorporates it into nascent VLDL; excess α-tocopherol, other tocopherols and tocotrienols are secreted in the bile. Adequate Intake for adults 13 mg/day α-tocopherol for men and 11 mg/day for women.
